builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Sightline: Calibrated Data-Flow Summaries for LLM-Integrated Applications
summary: It replaces over-approximating taint analysis (every output tainted by every prompt placeholder) and costly second-model labeling with per-call data-flow summaries read from a single recorded forward pass, learned from labels and calibrated to a chosen missed-flow rate. Cost is one forward pass per analyzed call plus a labeled calibration set per call-site distribution; it adds an analysis dependency outside the model-serving path. It can fail under distribution shift (calibration guarantees hold only when deployment is exchangeable with calibration), and the no-reading-no-flow result is a first-order approximation that faint attention or sensitivity can violate.
rationale: It is a program-analysis tool for taint tracking in LLM-integrated code, relevant only if the reader builds static analysis or information-flow control for LLM agents, not for standard production LLM serving.
technique: Calibrated data-flow summaries for LLM call taint analysis

claims.statement: It replaces over-approximating taint analysis (every output tainted by every prompt placeholder) and costly second-model labeling with per-call data-flow summaries read from a single recorded forward pass, learned from labels and calibrated to a chosen missed-flow rate. Cost is one forward pass per analyzed call plus a labeled calibration set per call-site distribution; it adds an analysis dependency outside the model-serving path. It can fail under distribution shift (calibration guarantees hold only when deployment is exchangeable with calibration), and the no-reading-no-flow result is a first-order approximation that faint attention or sensitivity can violate.
At 1% missed-flow calibration, prunes 43.9-65.6% of spurious taint flows, 1.6-2.6x more than the best baseline; improves analysis precision, not inference cost or quality.
